method_card.title: Bond Energy Calculations
steps: Count every bond: multiply each bond energy by how many of that bond there are.
Add the reactant bond energies for the total broken; add the product bond energies for the total made.
Negative means exothermic (energy out); positive means endothermic (energy in).
method_card.content:
ΔH = bonds broken − bonds made. Breaking bonds takes energy in (endothermic); making bonds gives energy out (exothermic).

Count carefully: multiply each bond energy by the number of those bonds (4 C–H in CH₄, not 1). Add the reactant bonds for broken, the product bonds for made, then subtract.

A negative answer means energy is released overall (exothermic); a positive answer means energy is absorbed (endothermic).

exam_context.frequency: Common: often appears as a 4 to 5 mark structured question

gold.display: Calculate the overall energy change for the combustion of ethene: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C=C = 614, C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

misconceptions.message: C₂H₄ has 4 C–H bonds (2 on each carbon), not 2. Using 2 C–H makes broken = 2934 and gives −2134 by mistake.

gold.hint: Break C=C, 4 C–H and 3 O=O; make 4 C=O and 4 O–H.

guided_steps.say: Break the reactant bonds: C₂H₄ has 1 C=C and 4 C–H; then 3 O=O.

guided_steps.hint: Ethene has 4 C–H bonds, two on each carbon.
3 × O=O = 1494; add the C=C too.

guided_steps.say: Make the product bonds: 2CO₂ has 4 C=O, 2H₂O has 4 O–H.

guided_steps.hint: Two CO₂ molecules, two C=O bonds each.
Add the water bonds.
Subtract made from broken.
Adding ΔH back should return the broken energy.
guided_steps.done: Returns 3760, so ΔH = −1308 kJ/mol is right.

gold.display: Calculate the overall energy change for the combustion of ethane: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. Bond energies: C–C = 347, C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol. Give the answer per mole of C₂H₆ (divide your total by 2).

misconceptions.message: The equation burns 2 mol of C₂H₆, so divide the whole ΔH by 2: −2856 ÷ 2 = −1428 kJ/mol. Leaving it as −2856 forgets the per-mole step.

gold.hint: Work out ΔH for the whole equation, then divide by 2 for one mole.

guided_steps.say: This equation burns 2 moles of ethane. Work out ΔH for the whole equation, then divide by 2.

guided_steps.hint: Two C₂H₆ molecules, 6 C–H each.
Total energy to break all reactant bonds.

guided_steps.say: Now the bonds made: 4CO₂ has 8 C=O, 6H₂O has 12 O–H.

guided_steps.hint: Four CO₂ molecules, two C=O each.
Total energy released making product bonds.
Broken minus made for the full equation.
Divide by 2 because the equation burns 2 mol.
Multiplying back by 2 should give the whole-equation ΔH.
guided_steps.done: Returns the whole-equation ΔH, so −1428 kJ/mol per mole of ethane is right.

gold.display: The overall energy change for a reaction is −285 kJ/mol. The total energy to break bonds in the reactants is 1845 kJ. Calculate the total energy released when new bonds form in the products.

misconceptions.message: made = broken − ΔH = 1845 − (−285) = 1845 + 285 = 2130 kJ. Doing 1845 + (−285) = 1560 mishandles the double negative.
Subtracting −285 means adding 285: 1845 + 285 = 2130 kJ.

gold.hint: Rearrange to made = broken − ΔH, and mind the double negative.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange ΔH = broken − made to made = broken − ΔH.

guided_steps.pre: ΔH is −285, so made = 1845 − (−285). Subtracting a negative adds it: 1845 +
guided_steps.hint: Two minus signs together become a plus.
Add.
This should return the given ΔH.
guided_steps.done: That is the given ΔH, so made = 2130 kJ is right.

gold.display: A reaction has ΔH = +140 kJ/mol. The energy released forming product bonds is 1380 kJ. Calculate the total energy needed to break all reactant bonds.

misconceptions.message: broken = ΔH + made = 140 + 1380 = 1520 kJ. Doing made − ΔH = 1240 subtracts when you should add.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange ΔH = broken − made to broken = ΔH + made.

guided_steps.pre: ΔH is +140 and made is 1380, so broken = 140 +
guided_steps.hint: Add the made energy to ΔH.
Add.
This should return the given ΔH.
guided_steps.done: That is the given ΔH, so broken = 1520 kJ is right.

gold.display: Reaction A has ΔH = −184 kJ/mol. Reaction B has ΔH = −814 kJ/mol. Which reaction releases more energy per mole?
gold.hint: The more negative the energy change, the more energy is released.

misconceptions.message: −814 is more negative than −184, so Reaction B releases more energy. A larger negative number means more exothermic.
Compare the size of the negative values: 814 > 184, so Reaction B releases more energy per mole.

gold.display: When 2 mol of hydrogen burns (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O), 486 kJ of energy is released. Calculate the energy released per gram of hydrogen. (Mr of H₂ = 2, so 1 mol of H₂ has a mass of 2 g.)
gold.hint: Find the mass of 2 mol of H₂ in grams, then divide the energy by that mass.

misconceptions.message: Per gram, not per mole: 2 mol of H₂ weighs 4 g, so 486 ÷ 4 = 121.5 kJ/g. Dividing by 2 mol instead gives 243 kJ/mol, a different quantity.

guided_steps.say: When 2 mol of H₂ burns, 486 kJ is released. First find the mass of 2 mol of H₂.

guided_steps.pre: 1 mol of H₂ weighs 2 g, so 2 mol weighs 2 × 2 =
guided_steps.hint: Multiply moles by the mass of one mole.
Divide the energy by the mass in grams.
Multiplying back should return the total energy.
guided_steps.done: Returns 486 kJ, so 121.5 kJ/g is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the total energy needed to break all bonds in the reactants for: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242 kJ/mol.
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{total broken} = \text{sum of all bond energies in reactants}\)

misconceptions.message: Only the reactant bonds are broken. Adding the product bonds too gives 436 + 242 + 862 = 1540, which is wrong. Broken = 436 + 242 = 678 kJ.

bronze.hint: Only add the reactant bonds: H–H plus Cl–Cl.

guided_steps.say: Break only the reactant bonds. There are two: one H–H and one Cl–Cl.

guided_steps.hint: That is the H–H bond energy.
That is the Cl–Cl bond energy.
Add the two bond energies.
guided_steps.done: That is the total energy to break the reactant bonds: 678 kJ.

bronze.display: Calculate the total energy released when all bonds are made in the products for: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–Cl = 431 kJ/mol.
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{total made} = \text{sum of all bond energies in products}\)

misconceptions.message: There are 2 HCl molecules, so 2 × H–Cl = 862 kJ. Using just one H–Cl (431) forgets the coefficient.

bronze.hint: Two HCl molecules means two H–Cl bonds, so double it.

guided_steps.say: Two HCl molecules form, so two H–Cl bonds are made.

guided_steps.hint: That is the H–Cl bond energy.
Multiply by the number of bonds.
Divide by 2 to undo.
guided_steps.done: Back to one H–Cl bond, so 862 kJ is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the overall energy change (ΔH) for: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431 kJ/mol.

misconceptions.message: ΔH = broken − made, not made − broken. 678 − 862 = −184 kJ/mol. Doing 862 − 678 = 184 flips the sign.
The answer is negative (−184), so the reaction is exothermic: energy is given out.

guided_steps.say: First find the energy to break the reactant bonds, then the energy released making the product bonds.

guided_steps.hint: Add the reactant bonds.
Two HCl molecules, so double.
Subtract made from broken; the answer is negative.
Adding ΔH back to made should give broken.
guided_steps.done: Returns the broken energy, so ΔH = −184 kJ/mol is right.

bronze.display: Is the reaction H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl exothermic or endothermic? (ΔH = −184 kJ/mol)

misconceptions.message: A negative ΔH means exothermic: more energy is released making new bonds than is needed to break the old ones.

bronze.hint: A negative energy change means energy is given out.

bronze.display: Calculate the overall energy change for: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Bond energies: H–H = 436, O=O = 498, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

misconceptions.message: 2H₂O has 4 O–H bonds, not 2. Using 2 × 464 = 928 gives +442, the wrong answer. Made = 4 × 464 = 1856 kJ.

bronze.hint: Count 2 H–H and 1 O=O to break, and 4 O–H made.

guided_steps.say: Break every reactant bond: 2 H–H bonds and 1 O=O bond.

guided_steps.hint: Two H₂ molecules, so double.
Add the single O=O bond energy.

guided_steps.say: Now the product bonds. 2H₂O has 4 O–H bonds.

guided_steps.hint: Four O–H bonds in two water molecules.
Subtract made from broken.
Adding ΔH back should return the broken energy.
guided_steps.done: Returns 1370, so ΔH = −486 kJ/mol is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the overall energy change for: H₂ + Br₂ → 2HBr. Bond energies: H–H = 436, Br–Br = 193, H–Br = 366 kJ/mol.

misconceptions.message: There are 2 HBr molecules, so 2 × H–Br = 732 kJ. Using one H–Br (366) gives 263 by mistake. ΔH = 629 − 732 = −103 kJ/mol.

bronze.hint: Break H–H and Br–Br, make two H–Br bonds.

guided_steps.say: Break the reactant bonds: one H–H and one Br–Br.

guided_steps.hint: Add the two reactant bonds.

guided_steps.say: Make the product bonds: 2 H–Br.

guided_steps.hint: Two HBr molecules, so double.
Subtract made from broken.
Adding ΔH back should return the broken energy.
guided_steps.done: Returns 629, so ΔH = −103 kJ/mol is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the overall energy change for: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. Bond energies: N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391 kJ/mol.

misconceptions.message: 2NH₃ has 6 N–H bonds (3 per molecule × 2). Using 3 N–H (1173) gives 1080, the wrong answer.

bronze.hint: Break one N≡N and three H–H, make six N–H bonds.

guided_steps.say: Break the reactant bonds: 1 N≡N and 3 H–H bonds.

guided_steps.hint: Three H₂ molecules.
Add the single N≡N bond energy.

guided_steps.say: Make the product bonds: 2NH₃ has 6 N–H bonds (3 per molecule).

guided_steps.hint: Six N–H bonds in total.
Subtract made from broken.
Adding ΔH back should return the broken energy.
guided_steps.done: Returns 2253, so ΔH = −93 kJ/mol is right.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many O–H bonds are formed in total?
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{count all bonds in all product molecules}\)

misconceptions.message: Each water molecule has 2 O–H bonds and there are 2 molecules, so 2 × 2 = 4 bonds. Counting 2 forgets one molecule.
Count bonds, not molecules: 2H₂O is 2 molecules × 2 O–H bonds each = 4 O–H bonds.

bronze.hint: Two water molecules, each with two O–H bonds.

guided_steps.say: Count the product molecules: 2H₂O is two water molecules.

guided_steps.pre: O–H bonds in one water molecule =
guided_steps.hint: Water is H–O–H: two O–H bonds.
Multiply bonds per molecule by the number of molecules.
Divide back by the number of molecules.
guided_steps.done: Two O–H bonds per water molecule, so 4 in total.

silver.display: Calculate the overall energy change for the combustion of methane: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

Two O₂ molecules.

Subtract made from broken.

silver.display: The combustion of methane (CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O) has ΔH = −814 kJ/mol. The total energy to break all bonds in the reactants is 2648 kJ. Calculate the total energy released when bonds in the products are formed.

silver.hint: Rearrange ΔH = broken − made to made = broken − ΔH.

guided_steps.pre: ΔH is −814, so made = 2648 − (−814). Subtracting a negative adds it: 2648 +

Add.
This should return the given ΔH.

silver.display: A reaction has bonds broken = 1845 kJ and bonds made = 2130 kJ. Calculate ΔH and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

misconceptions.message: ΔH = broken − made = 1845 − 2130 = −285 kJ/mol (exothermic). Doing 2130 − 1845 = 285 flips the sign.
More energy is released making bonds (2130) than breaking them (1845), so ΔH is negative: exothermic.

guided_steps.say: Find ΔH = broken − made, then decide exothermic or endothermic.

guided_steps.hint: How much bigger the made value is.

guided_steps.pre: More is made than broken, so ΔH is negative: 1845 − 2130 =
guided_steps.hint: Broken minus made comes out negative here.
Adding ΔH back should return bonds broken.
guided_steps.done: Returns bonds broken, so ΔH = −285 kJ/mol (exothermic).

silver.display: A reaction has bonds broken = 1520 kJ and bonds made = 1380 kJ. Calculate ΔH and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

misconceptions.message: ΔH = broken − made = 1520 − 1380 = +140 kJ/mol. Doing made − broken = −140 flips the sign. Positive means endothermic.

guided_steps.say: ΔH = broken − made, with broken = 1520 and made = 1380.

guided_steps.hint: Broken minus made; here it is positive.

guided_steps.pre: Positive ΔH means endothermic. Check by adding back: 1380 + 140 =
guided_steps.hint: Made plus ΔH should return bonds broken.

guided_steps.pre: And bonds made should be broken − ΔH: 1520 − 140 =
guided_steps.hint: This should return bonds made.
guided_steps.done: Returns bonds made, so ΔH = +140 kJ/mol (endothermic) is right.

guided_steps.pre: O–H bonds in one water molecule =

silver.display: A student calculates ΔH for a reaction and gets +320 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?
options: More energy is released making bonds than breaking bonds
More energy is absorbed breaking bonds than making bonds
The reaction gives out heat to the surroundings

misconceptions.message: Positive ΔH means more energy is absorbed breaking bonds than released making them. The reaction is endothermic: it takes in heat from the surroundings.

silver.hint: Positive means energy is taken in overall.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation, values given: add the reactant bonds, add the product bonds, subtract.
problem_bank.silver_description: Count several bonds per molecule, or rearrange ΔH = broken − made to find a missing total.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step: many bonds to count, a per-mole division, or a per-gram comparison.

worked_examples.question: Calculate the overall energy change for: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H = 436 kJ/mol, Cl–Cl = 242 kJ/mol, H–Cl = 431 kJ/mol.

steps.label: Step 1: Bonds broken
steps.content:
CH₄: 4 × C–H = 4 × 413 = 1652 kJ
2O₂: 2 × O=O = 2 × 498 = 996 kJ
Total broken = 2648 kJ

steps.label: Step 2: Bonds made
steps.content:
CO₂: 2 × C=O = 2 × 803 = 1606 kJ
2H₂O: 4 × O–H = 4 × 464 = 1856 kJ
Total made = 3462 kJ

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: ΔH = −814 kJ/mol (exothermic: more energy released making bonds than absorbed breaking them)

worked_examples.question: Calculate the overall energy change for the combustion of methane: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

steps.label: Step 1: Bonds broken
steps.content:
C₂H₄: 1 × C=C = 614, 4 × C–H = 1652. Total = 2266 kJ
3O₂: 3 × O=O = 1494 kJ
Total broken = 3760 kJ

steps.label: Step 2: Bonds made
steps.content:
2CO₂: 4 × C=O = 3212 kJ
2H₂O: 4 × O–H = 1856 kJ

worked_examples.question: Calculate the energy change for the combustion of ethene: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C=C = 614, C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

bronze.title: Bronze: add up, then subtract
steps: Every bond has an energy. Breaking a bond needs energy in; making a bond gives energy out.
Add all the bond energies in the reactants (bonds broken) and all in the products (bonds made). Multiply each by how many of that bond there are.
ΔH = bonds broken − bonds made. A negative answer means the reaction gives out energy (exothermic).

example.question: Calculate ΔH for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431 kJ/mol.

silver.title: Silver: count carefully or rearrange
steps: Molecules can hold several of the same bond: CH₄ has 4 C–H bonds, 2H₂O has 4 O–H bonds. Multiply each bond energy by its count before adding.
If the question gives ΔH and one total, rearrange: made = broken − ΔH, or broken = ΔH + made.
Read the sign: negative ΔH is exothermic (energy out), positive ΔH is endothermic (energy in).

example.question: Calculate ΔH for CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

gold.title: Gold: multi-step problems
steps: Big molecules mean many bonds: draw them out and count every C–H, C=C, C=O and O–H before you multiply.
If the equation shows more than one mole of fuel, find ΔH for the whole equation, then divide by the number of moles for a per-mole answer.
To compare fuels per gram, divide each energy change by the mass of that many moles (mass = moles × Mr).

example.question: Calculate ΔH for the combustion of ethene: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bond energies: C=C = 614, C–H = 413, O=O = 498, C=O = 803, O–H = 464 kJ/mol.

opener.label: Before any chemistry
opener.display:
You dismantle an old shed and build a fence from the reclaimed wood.
Taking the shed apart costs you £678.
Selling the finished fence earns you £862.

steps.pre: Overall, how many £ better off are you? 862 − 678 =
steps.hint: Take the cost away from what you earn.
steps.say: A money puzzle first, no chemistry needed.

steps.pre: Chemists write the change as cost − earning, in the same order every time: 678 − 862 =
steps.hint: Cost first, then take away the earning. The answer comes out negative.
steps.say: Notice the size is the same, £184, but written this way it is negative.

You gained £184, and chemists write that gain as ΔH = −184 kJ/mol. Breaking bonds is the cost (energy in), making bonds is the earning (energy out), and ΔH = bonds broken − bonds made. A negative answer means energy was released: the reaction is exothermic. That is the whole method.

bronze.label: Together: your first one
bronze.display: Calculate ΔH for H₂ + F₂ → 2HF. Bond energies: H–H = 436, F–F = 158, H–F = 568 kJ/mol.

steps.pre: Break the reactant bonds: H–H + F–F = 436 + 158 =
steps.hint: Add the two reactant bond energies.
steps.say: Break every bond in the reactants first.

steps.pre: Make the product bonds: 2 HF means 2 × H–F = 2 × 568 =
steps.hint: Two HF molecules form, so double the H–F energy.
steps.say: Now the bonds made in the two product molecules.

steps.hint: Subtract made from broken; it comes out negative.
Adding ΔH back to made should return the broken energy.
steps.done: Returns 594, the broken energy, so ΔH = −542 kJ/mol (exothermic). That was the whole method.

silver.label: Together: counting and the sign
silver.display: Calculate ΔH for N₂ + O₂ → 2NO. Bond energies: N≡N = 945, O=O = 498, N=O = 630 kJ/mol.

steps.pre: Break the reactant bonds: N≡N + O=O = 945 + 498 =
steps.hint: Add the two reactant bond energies.
steps.say: One N≡N triple bond and one O=O double bond break.

steps.pre: Make the product bonds: 2 NO means 2 × N=O = 2 × 630 =
steps.hint: Two NO molecules form, so double the N=O energy.
steps.say: Two NO molecules form, each with one N=O bond.

steps.hint: Subtract made from broken; here it comes out positive.
Adding ΔH back to made should return the broken energy.
steps.done: Returns 1443, and the positive sign means this reaction is endothermic. Counting the bonds and reading the sign was the point.
